en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew leaves the object unstated.

01.r: Joins this verse to the list; the object marker points to 'your slaves'.
01.n: The Hebrew is 'and' with the small word that marks a definite direct object, which has no English equivalent; both are counted here with 'your slaves'.

02.r: The male slaves a household owns.
02.n: Gesenius: a servant, who among the Hebrews was commonly a slave. These belong to the people's own households, so 'slaves'; the translations say 'menservants'.

03.r: Adds the next item, with the object marker again.

04.r: The women who serve in a household.
04.n: Gesenius: a maid-servant, a household servant; the brief's lexicon adds 'slavegirl'. A different word from the one for male slaves, so our English keeps them apart.

05.r: Adds the next item, with the object marker again.

06.r: The grown but unmarried young men of the families.
06.n: Gesenius: a youth, a young man of mature age but unmarried, citing this verse. The Greek reads 'your herds' here instead, and the BSB follows it with 'cattle'.

07.r: The king picks the strongest and finest.
07.n: Literally 'the good ones', as with the best fields in 1 Samuel 8:14. Placed after the young men, it most naturally describes them; the Geneva says 'the chiefe of your yong men'.

08.r: Adds the last item, with the object marker again.

09.r: The donkeys used for carrying and farm work.
09.n: BDB: (he-)ass, as valuable property alongside oxen, sheep, camels and slaves, used for riding, as a beast of burden, and in tillage.

10.r: The king will take them from their owners.
10.n: The same common verb for 'take' that runs through Samuel's list.

11.r: He will set them to labour for him.
11.n: The ordinary verb 'do, make'; Gesenius gives the proper sense as to labour, to work about anything. Literally 'and he will make (them) for his work'. A perfect with 'and', carrying on the future; YLT renders it 'hath prepared'.

12.r: Work done for the king, not for their own households.
12.n: Gesenius: properly service, hence work prescribed to anyone. The brief's lexicon includes 'service, use' and 'public business'; the BSB says 'his own use'.

_extra.11: καὶ (and): the Greek makes 'the good' a separate item, 'and the good ones', where the Hebrew describes the young men.

03.n: κα stands for καί, and; the text as given is cut short.

04.n: δούλη, female slave: the feminine of δοῦλος.

06.n: βουκόλιον, a herd of cattle, where the Hebrew has 'your young men'. The Greek translators likely read a different Hebrew word here; the BSB follows them with 'cattle'.

07.n: ἀγαθός, good: in the Greek, 'the good things' stand as their own item.

11.n: ἀποδεκατόω, 'he will tithe', where the Hebrew has 'he will use (them)': the Greek reads the tithing of 1 Samuel 8:15 and 8:17 into this verse too.
